messages.author: 6fb6fd6543d77a99
messages.subject: simulating data for multiple groups
parts:
Hi all,

I was trying to simulate data for 2 groups using the function simulateData and got the error message below. I am not sure if i am doing the correct thing in terms of specifying the population model. Any suggestion will be greatly appreciated.

Cheers,
Yonghao

library(lavaan)

model <- '
f =~ 1*x1 + 1*x2 + 1*x3
f ~~ c(0.5,0.3)*f
x1 ~~ 0.3*x1
x2 ~~ 0.3*x2
x3 ~~ 0.3*x3
'

my.df <- simulateData(model, sample.nobs=c(100,100),group.label=c('1','2'))

Error in lavaanify(model = model, meanstructure = meanstructure, int.ov.free = int.ov.free,  :
  lavaan ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier () of element f~~f

Hello Yves,

I'm not sure whether this is another bug in simulateData(), or if I need to specify means a different way.  I'm specifying means much larger than zero, but the fitted values and simulated data have means of (close to) zero.

model <- "
y ~ 3 + 0.5*x # regression with intercept (mean Y with X = 0)
y ~~ 2*y      # residual variance of Y
x ~~ 1.5*x    # variance of X
x ~ 10        # mean of X
"

> fitted(sem(model, fixed.x = FALSE))
$cov
  y     x   
y 2.375     
x 0.750 1.500

$mean
y x
0 0

> data1 <- simulateData(model, meanstructure = TRUE, sample.nobs = 1000)

0.05761786 0.02847802
> var(data1)
          y         x
y 2.0991539 0.6607919
x 0.6607919 1.5143379

Thanks,

Terry

messages.subject: Re: simulating data for multiple groups
parts:
On 11/03/2012 10:32 PM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
> Hello Yves,
>
> I'm not sure whether this is another bug in simulateData(), or if I need
> to specify means a different way. I'm specifying means much larger than
> zero, but the fitted values and simulated data have means of (close to)
> zero.
>
> model <- "
> y ~ 3 + 0.5*x # regression with intercept (mean Y with X = 0)
> y ~~ 2*y # residual variance of Y
> x ~~ 1.5*x # variance of X
> x ~ 10 # mean of X
> "

It is the model syntax: 'x ~ 10' is (currently) not legal syntax. You
need to write: 'x ~ 10*1'.

Yves.
